title: 2026 General Election — Monterey Park, CA
description: California's November 3 general election as it appears on Monterey Park ballots: Governor and the other statewide offices, U.S. House District 28, Assembly District 49, the Los Angeles County Sheriff runoff, Monterey Park city races, 14 statewide propositions, two county charter amendments and two city measures. School and special-district measures are not included. California has no U.S. Senate race in 2026. Candidates and ballot designations are from the Secretary of State's certified list (Aug 27, 2026).

offices.title: U.S. Representative, District 28
offices.description: 2-year term. Monterey Park is entirely in District 28 under the Proposition 50 (2025) congressional map.

offices.title: Governor
offices.description: Chief executive of California. 4-year term; Gavin Newsom is term-limited.

offices.title: Board of Equalization, District 3
offices.description: District 3 is all of Los Angeles County. 4-year term.

offices.title: State Assembly, District 49
offices.description: 2-year term. Monterey Park is in Assembly District 49. (Its State Senate seat, District 25, is not up in 2026.)

offices.title: Los Angeles County Sheriff
offices.description: Nonpartisan runoff; no candidate won a majority in the June 2 primary. A rematch of 2022.

measures.title: Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs
measures.description: Authorizes $11.25 billion in state general obligation bonds for housing affordability programs, including multifamily rental housing, mortgages for veterans, supportive housing, preservation of existing affordable housing, and downpayment assistance.
measures.yesMeans: The state could borrow $11.25 billion to support veterans and affordable housing.
measures.noMeans: The state could not borrow $11.25 billion to support veterans and affordable housing.
measures.fiscalImpact: Increased state cost of $500 million to $600 million annually for about 25 years to repay the housing bond.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by the Legislature

measures.title: Increases State's Rainy Day Fund
measures.description: Increases California's Rainy Day Fund, approved by voters in 2014, to provide funding for education, health care, public safety, and other essential services during economic downturns.
measures.yesMeans: Rules for building state budget reserves and paying down extra state debts would change. As a result, state budget reserves would be higher. The state also would be required to make extra debt payments for longer.
measures.noMeans: Rules for building state budget reserves and paying down extra state debts would not change.
measures.fiscalImpact: State budget reserves would be higher.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by the Legislature

measures.title: Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes
measures.description: Makes permanent existing voter-approved tax rates for individuals earning over $371,000 (adjusted annually for inflation). Allocates tax revenues to public education.
measures.yesMeans: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would become permanent instead of expiring in 2031.
measures.noMeans: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would expire in 2031.
measures.fiscalImpact: Maintains $5 billion to $15 billion of annual state income tax revenue by making a temporary tax increase on high-income earners permanent instead of letting it expire in 2031.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns
measures.description: Repeals prohibition on state and local governments offering public funding of candidate election campaigns. Public funding programs may not use funds earmarked for education, transportation, or public safety.
measures.yesMeans: State and local governments could create public campaign financing programs for public office candidates, subject to limits on which public funds could be used, how the public funds could be used, and who could receive them.
measures.noMeans: State and most local governments would remain unable to create public campaign finance programs for public office candidates.
measures.fiscalImpact: Ongoing costs to the state of a few hundred thousand dollars each year for the Fair Political Practices Commission to answer questions from state and local governments about public campaign finance programs.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by the Legislature

measures.title: Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers
measures.description: Under current law, voters elect replacement candidates at the same time as the recall election. This measure instead fills recall vacancies by subsequent special election or appointment.
measures.yesMeans: Recall elections would no longer include a question about who should fill the vacancy. Instead, vacancies typically would be filled through special elections or appointments, depending on the office and timing.
measures.noMeans: Voters would continue to be asked who should fill the vacancy as part of recall elections.
measures.fiscalImpact: Net fiscal effect unknown. In the event of a recall, savings or costs of millions of dollars to administer the election depending on the office recalled.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by the Legislature

measures.title: Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes
measures.description: Authorizes $25 billion in bonds to offer eligible buyers fixed-rate mortgages for up to 17% of purchase price of a newly constructed home priced below about $1.5 million. Borrowers must be California residents, occupy the home, meet income limits, and pay at least 3% down. Bonds repaid by mortgage payments, not State.
measures.yesMeans: The state would create a new homebuying assistance program. The state could sell up to $25 billion in revenue bonds to fund the program. Bonds would be paid back by homeowners’ payments on their home loans.
measures.noMeans: The state would not be required to create a new homebuying assistance program.
measures.fiscalImpact: No direct state or local costs.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research
measures.description: Authorizes $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds for immunology and immunotherapy research, half to a single University of California-affiliated nonprofit medical research institute, half to research grants.
measures.yesMeans: The state could borrow $8.4 billion to support medical research in immunology and immunotherapy conducted by California research institutes and universities.
measures.noMeans: The state could not borrow $8.4 billion to support medical research in immunology and immunotherapy conducted by California research institutes and universities.
measures.fiscalImpact: Increased state cost of $500 million to $600 million annually for about 20 years to repay the research bond, with some or all of the cost offset if the funded research generates revenue.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification
measures.description: Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification.
measures.yesMeans: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
measures.noMeans: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
measures.fiscalImpact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers
measures.description: Imposes 5% tax on certain taxpayers with assets over $1 billion; revenue primarily for health care. Exempts revenues from constitutional requirements for school funding and spending limit.
measures.yesMeans: The state would collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
measures.noMeans: The state would not collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
measures.fiscalImpact: Temporary revenue increase of tens of billions of dollars spread over several years from wealth tax on billionaires. Possible ongoing decrease of less than $1 billion per year in income tax revenue from billionaires.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes
measures.description: Nullifies state taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that exempt their revenues from voter-approved state spending limit. Requires pre-election and recurring audits of programs funded by new special taxes.
measures.yesMeans: When special taxes are proposed by voter initiatives, the California State Auditor would review programs funded by the tax before the initiative appears on the ballot. The California State Auditor also would regularly review programs funded by special taxes approved by voters or the Legislature. In addition, the state might not be able to exclude any new special tax spending from its spending limit.
measures.noMeans: The California State Auditor’s responsibility to review government programs would not change. The state spending limit requirements would not change.
measures.fiscalImpact: The net fiscal effect is unknown as it depends on future decisions by voters, the Legislature, and other policymakers.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes
measures.description: Prohibits any new state tax (1) imposed on the ownership of personal property (all things people own other than real estate), or (2) that applies retroactively based on taxpayer’s past activities. Nullifies taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that conflict with this measure.
measures.yesMeans: The state could not establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
measures.noMeans: The state would continue to have the option to establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
measures.fiscalImpact: Possibility that tax revenues will not go up as much in the future.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services
measures.description: Limits voters’ ability to pass voter-proposed local special taxes by increasing percentage of votes needed to approve such ballot measures from a majority (over 50%) to two-thirds, beginning January 1, 2027.
measures.yesMeans: Certain local government taxes would require two-thirds approval by voters.
measures.noMeans: Certain local government taxes could continue to be approved by voters with a majority vote.
measures.fiscalImpact: Possibility that local government tax revenues will not go up as much in the future due to a higher vote threshold for certain taxes.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by the Legislature

measures.title: Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services
measures.description: Imposes penalties on nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers (community clinics providing primary care to medically underserved areas and populations) that spend less than 90% of revenue on “program services” advancing their charitable purpose, including but not limited to patient services.
measures.yesMeans: Certain private nonprofit health care clinics would have to spend at least 90 percent of their revenue each year on providing health care services.
measures.noMeans: The new requirement on health care clinic spending would not go into effect.
measures.fiscalImpact: Increased state costs in the low tens of millions of dollars per year, covered by fees.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects
measures.description: Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals.
measures.yesMeans: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures. For example, new procedures would tighten time limits for environmental review and reduce the scope of what courts can consider when reviewing legal challenges.
measures.noMeans: Public and private projects would continue to use existing project review and court challenge procedures.
measures.fiscalImpact: Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees. Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects.
measures.placedBy: Put on the ballot by petition signatures

measures.title: Los Angeles County Charter Amendment: Good-Faith Negotiation and Binding Arbitration for Public Safety Employee Disputes
measures.description: Would amend the County Charter to prohibit strikes by district attorney investigators, medical examiners, lifeguards, their supervisors, and non-administrative civilian employees of the Fire, Sheriff's and Medical Examiner departments; restate existing good-faith negotiation obligations; and set up impartial binding arbitration for labor disputes with certified public safety employee organizations. Majority vote.

measures.title: County of Los Angeles Ethics Commission and Community Investment Budget Allocation Charter Amendment
measures.description: Would amend the County Charter to give the county Ethics Commission, Office of Ethics Compliance and Ethics Compliance Officer more independence and structure (appointments, qualifications, terms, duties), and continue the county's commitment to community investment and alternatives to incarceration. Majority vote.

measures.title: Create HOME Housing Overlays in Monterey Park
measures.description: Would amend the city's Land Use Element to create a Housing Overlay Mixed Environments (HOME) designation allowing housing (multifamily, townhomes, condos, mixed use) in identified commercial and industrial areas. It would not approve any project by itself, would not apply in R-1 or R-2 zones, and keeps the city's ban on data centers.

measures.title: Transient Occupancy Tax
measures.description: Would raise the hotel/motel guest tax from 13% to 14% and set a 16% rate for short-term rental guests, raising about $600,000 a year for city services until ended by voters.
